overview: Black adopts a set-up of pawns on the sixth rank (g6, f6, e6, d6) with the king's bishop on g7 and the king's knight on h6, aiming for a compact, flexible position. The input's most played line is 2.d4 g6 3.c4 f6. White gets a big centre and space; Black waits and breaks later with ...c6, ...e5 or ...d5. The set-up can be played against almost anything.

white_ideas.idea: Take the centre with d4, c4, Nc3 and Be3 and gain space.
Attack Black's compact set-up with an early Bxh6 or h4-h5 and a kingside pawn push.

black_ideas.idea: Hold the sixth-rank pawn wall and fianchetto Bg7, then play ...c6, ...e5 or ...d5.
Keep the position compact and counter in the centre when White overextends.

typical_structures.structure: Black pawns on d6, e6, f6, g6 with the Bg7 and the knight on h6 against a big White centre.

character.notes: Compact, passive and difficult to crack, with few early tactics, but White has an easy space edge.

soundness.notes: Passive but defensible, with no clear refutation.

structure.notes: Black keeps pawns back and the centre undecided, waiting to break later.

approach.notes: A set-up you can play against almost anything, as the site's anchor says.

level.notes: Flexible plans and timing of the breaks take understanding; not a beginner choice.

plan_phrases: hedgehog-style pawn wall on the sixth rank
